paper_title: Knowledge Crosswords Geometric Knowledge Reasoning with Large Language   Models
caption: Problem distribution based on the correctness under the w/ knowledge and w/o knowledge settings using CoT and . The results indicate that while easier problems are mainly hindered by a lack of knowledge, the bottleneck for hard problems lies in geometric knowledge reasoning abilities.
model_annotation: This chart depicts the distribution of problems categorized by difficulty—easy, medium, and hard—based on correctness with and without knowledge, using Chain-of-Thought (CoT) prompting. Each of the three charts, representing the difficulty levels, contains four slices. The slices are labeled “N+K+”, “N-K+”, “N-K-”, and “N+K-”, and are colored teal, yellow, orange, and red respectively. The “easy” chart shows proportions of approximately 40.6%, 3.3%, 45.9%, and 10.1% for the teal, red, yellow, and orange slices, respectively. The “medium” chart shows proportions of 44.6%, 3.9%, 44.3%, and 7.2% for the teal, red, yellow, and orange slices, respectively. Lastly, the "hard" chart displays proportions of 36.2%, 20.1%, 36.8%, and 7.0% for the teal, yellow, orange, and red slices. A legend identifying the slice labels and their corresponding colors is provided in the “hard” chart. Percentage labels are included directly within each slice of all three charts. The slices in each chart appear to be ordered clockwise, with the teal slice generally positioned at the top.
